body.statement:
For every admissible \(k\) and every \(n\geq4\),
\[
 D_k(n)\geq
 2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}.
\]
The lower bound is attained within the one-sink family by one original directed coefficient. At \(n=5\), the separate exact values are the sharper conclusions \(D_1(5)=3\) and \(D_k(5)=4\) for \(k\geq2\).
body.proof_tex:
Fix admissible \(k\) and \(n\ge4\), and put
\[
 j=\min\{k,\lfloor(n-4)/2\rfloor\}.
\tag{91}
\]
Then \(0\le j\le k\) and \(n\ge2j+4\).  Apply \(\mathrm{thm:large\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\) with budget \(j\).  Its one-sink graph-query belongs to \(\mathcal G_{n,j}\) and its original queried edge satisfies
\[
 d_{e^\star}(G^\star_{j,n})=2^{j+1}.
\tag{92}
\]
Because \(j\le k\), the member condition \(|D\setminus T|\le j\) implies \(|D\setminus T|\le k\), and hence
\[
 \mathcal G_{n,j}\subseteq\mathcal G_{n,k}
\tag{93}
\]
by \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\).  Taking the maximum defining \(D_k(n)\) in (92)--(93) gives
\[
 D_k(n)\ge2^{j+1}.
\]
For every integer \(n\ge4\),
\[
 \lfloor(n-4)/2\rfloor+1=\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor,
\]
and for nonnegative integers \(k,a\), \(\min\{k,a\}+1=\min\{k+1,a+1\}\).  Therefore
\[
 j+1=\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\},
\]
which proves
\[
 D_k(n)\ge2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}.
\]
The witness in (92) uses the original coefficient \(e^\star\).  The sharper five-vertex values \(D_1(5)=3\) and \(D_k(5)=4\) for \(k\ge2\) follow directly from \(\mathrm{thm:small\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\); they are separate because the one-sink envelope is not claimed sharp there.
body.justification: Class monotonicity turns the large-size one-sink construction into a certified lower bound at every size.
body.gap: The envelope need not be sharp in the remaining strip, as the sharper five-vertex cubic and quartic values demonstrate.
body.consumer: Any eventual all-size recurrence must dominate this explicit lower envelope.
